newsitem.title: USA: GE says positioned for record 1997 results.
newsitem.headline: GE says positioned for record 1997 results.

text.p: General Electric Co, reporting higher 1996 fourth quarter results, said Thursday it was "better positioned than ever" to deliver record results in 1997.
GE reported fourth quarter earnings per share of $1.26, up from $1.12 a year earlier. For the full year 1996, earnings were $4.40 a share, up from 1995's $3.90.
The earnings matched Wall Street's expectations. According to First Call, analysts' consensus estimates were $1.26 a share for the fourth quarter and $4.40 a share for the year.
In a statement, GE Chairman John Welch said earnings per share for the year increased 13 percent, and net income rose 11 percent to a record $7.28 billion.
Earnings per share grew faster than earnings because of the effects of a four-year, $13 billion share repurchase program initiated in December 1994.

Welch said revenues, including acquisitions, were a record $79.2 billion in 1996. The 13 percent rise from 1995 was driven primarily by GE Capital Services, increased global activities, higher sales of spare parts and services by GE equipment businesses, and revenue from the Summer Olympics televised by NBC.
Welch said the company was "confident that GE enters 1997 better positioned than ever to deliver another year of record results."
Revenues increased at nine of GE's 12 businesses last year, led by double-digit growth at GE Capital Services, NBC and Power Systems.
Welch said GE's 1996 operating margin rate was a record 14.8 percent of sales, up from 14.4 percent in 1995.
Nine businesses, led by Power Systems, NBC, Appliances, Medical Systems and Aircraft Engines, reported higher operating margins.
